verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's results docs describe both a Bayesian and a Frequentist engine, with metrics such as Chance to Win. The official repo lists CUPED, Sequential, Post-Stratification and SRM checks, which covers the variance-reduction part of the story. A maintainer comment also confirms the Bayesian engine. Community worries about peeking and significance alerts are general skepticism, not concrete contradictions. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of CUPED/post-stratification methodology (only a README bullet), and independent hands-on validation of the stats engine's correctness.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can trust a documented statistics engine (Bayesian or frequentist, with variance-reduction options) behind experiment results

citations.quote: What you will see will depend a little bit on whether you are using our Bayesian or our Frequentist engine
World class experiment stats engine (CUPED, Sequential, Bayesian, Post-Strat, Bandits, SRM checks).
Chance to Win tells you the probability that the variation is better.
We use a Bayesian statistics engine which is much more immune to peeking problems and Type I errors than frequentist approaches.
